title.narrative: Promoting Sustainable and Inclusive livelihood Project

description.narrative: The project is implemented by the Iringa Farmers' Cooperative Union (IFCU) in 30 selected Primary Cooperative Societies out of 62 across three districts and one municipality in Iringa Region, Tanzania. It targets 4,200 smallholder farmers (2,660 men, 1,540 women), including 760 youth, with additional indirect reach to over 22,000 community farmers. The project's main purpose is to enhance sustainable and inclusive livelihoods among cooperative members by strengthening governance, improving market access, and building climate resilience. It aims to empower women and youth, expand financial inclusion, and promote climate-responsive agricultural practices. Expected results include stronger cooperative institutions, increased participation of women and youth in leadership, improved access to financial and insurance services, reduced post-harvest losses, and enhanced productivity through agroecology and farmer-led research. Key activities include capacity building for cooperative leaders and members, establishing SACCOS at union and primary levels, facilitating access to insurance and reliable markets, promoting drought-tolerant crops, advocacy strengthening on land rights, and improving skills in post-harvest handling and value addition. The project operates in a context of weak governance, limited financial access, climate risks, and market exploitation, which the intervention is designed to address strategically.
